content.content:
Team error404.ai at the Atira EHL Challenge ("From RFQ to bid", challenge id `rfq`, event 10 Oct 2026, up to 5 people
per team). The agent lives in `agent/` and is built on the Atira starter kit. Keep the GitHub repo private.

## Status and layout

- `docs/plan.md`: framework decision (pydantic-ai on Qwen, no LangGraph, no browser-agent framework), module layout,
  site scouting notes and the roadmap v0 to v5. Read it first. Its scouting notes describe public-1 only: they inform
  generic helpers, they must never become hardcoded paths, labels, values or prompt text (the private final run uses
  other software, layouts and data).
- `agent/`: starter kit (`run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py`) plus the harness (`llm.py`, `extract.py`,
  `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `tracing.py`) and v1: `agent.py` `solve()` reads the brief (`briefing.py`), then
  `submit.py` signs a bid with every position omitted, fetching the contact address and TAN from the webmail.
  `calc.py` holds the deterministic bid rules (tested, not wired in yet). `agent.json` asks for 2 browsers.
- `dev/smoke.py`: the v0 check (one worker per site logs in and reads a page). From the repo root:
  `eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python dev/smoke.py [siteId ...]`
- Next: v2 to v4 for field points (research workers for spec, ERP, tender Q&A and mail, wired into `calc.py`). Use
  `git status` and `atira status` for the current state; do not trust dated numbers in this file.

## Tracking runs

Record every test run and submission; they go to `experiments/runs.jsonl` (append-only, `merge=union`, committed with
the change it measured). Local runs go to `experiments/local-runs.jsonl` (gitignored). `python3 dev/track.py report`
renders both to `docs/experiments.md` (gitignored). From the repo root:

```sh
dev/test-run.sh v1 "what changed" [experiment]    # sandbox test run, followed to the end, score recorded
dev/run-local.sh v1 "what changed" [experiment]   # local, headless; needs `atira models proxy`
python3 dev/track.py platform <sub_id> --version v1 --experiment NAME --note "..."   # after `atira submit`
```

`version` is the base being measured (v1, v2, ...); `experiment` names what a run varies on top of it (e.g.
`thinking-off-forms`, `model-<name>`, `4-browsers`), so variants of one version compare side by side. Environment
overrides (`AGENT_*`, `LLM_*`, `THINKING*`, `MAX_STEPS*`) are recorded, with secrets redacted. `atira test-run`
uploads untracked files too, so the recorded commit is a pointer; `atira package <id>` shows the exact upload.
When a run taught something (a failure mode, a speed-up, a score change), add a bullet to `docs/learned.md`. Notes
never contain credentials or values copied from the sites.

## Platform docs (source of truth; re-read, they change)

Base `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai`. Public pages (home, start, challenge, leaderboard, team profiles) are also
Markdown via `.md`; docs are `/docs/<name>.md`.

- `/start.md`, `/challenges/rfq.md` (29 bid rules, answer schema), `/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md`
- `/docs/fair-play.md`, `scoring.md`, `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `building-an-agent.md`, `cli.md`, `api.md`,
  `mcp.md`, `faq.md`, `demo-day.md`; `/openapi.json`, `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` (all docs in one file)
- Announcements need a token: `curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/v1/announcements`
- Submission deadline and prizes are not in the docs: ask the organizers. Demo day: best teams run live on stage, so
  keep a one-line start command (`atira test-run ./agent`) and a fallback recording.

The scouting logins are deliberately NOT stored here: run `atira scout`. Never write them, or anything copied from
the sites, into code, prompts, fixtures, notes or fallbacks.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer rejects or flags these)

- No hardcoded scenario values (tender refs, material numbers, prices, discounts, logins, TANs), not even as defaults,
  fallbacks or in prompts. Facts the brief states for every scenario (e.g. the sales director's mailbox) are fine.
- No pre-solving, by you or an AI assistant, put into the package. Hand-derived expectations stay outside `agent/`.
- Must be agentic: a model chooses where to go, what to search and what matters. Rejected: a fixed click path (model
  unused or only a fallback), or a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation.
  Allowed helpers: parse a page or document the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate,
  validate, retry, fill forms. Several agents and parallel browsers are fine.
- Only the platform API, the four sites and the model proxy; no local models; no own browsers in the sandbox (use the
  provided 1 to 4, tabs and contexts are free).
- Do not write notes meant to steer the reviewer. Outcomes: passed; flagged (runs, but hidden from the leaderboard
  until an organizer passes it); rejected (no runs).

## The task and its traps

One signed bid, entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with a TAN from the webmail. Site ids are
public-1 names; the private set renames and re-splits sites, so never branch code on siteId, URL or layout.

| Site | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| Tender portal | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (the hub: quantity changes, withdrawals, scoped spec amendments, Konditionsgruppe, packaging, commitment and setup-pool keys), configurator |
| Supplier portal | Buyer's spec and revisions (oldest shown first; use the one marked current) |
| ERP | Materials and status, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity and scales, pieces per carton, allocation mass |
| Webmail | Director's discount approval, TAN, authority mails (look-alikes, superseded, archive) |

Read all 29 rules in `challenges/rfq.md` before writing prompts or tools. Highest-impact traps:

- **Authority and time (21):** per key, the latest record dated no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender
  reference, from the right sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation + bidder mailbox domain). Future-dated and
  unrelated records never apply; a failed condition does not revive an older record.
- **no_bid (3, 8, 16):** if any position has no exactly matching active material (after amendments and the "nutzbarer
  Weg" derivation, rule 20), send `no_bid`, no positions, `total_net` 0 (schema still requires `discount_percent`; a
  conditional approval means 0 %). Omitting positions is not a substitute (rule 9).
- **Sign and submit:** saving alone scores nothing. Partial bids use "Position auslassen" and are still signed.
- **Per position vs per material:** price scales per position; stock pooled per material (15); delivery commitments
  per position, only if the material matches and pooled demand is within the inclusive ceiling (24).
- **Rounding:** HALF_UP, at the steps the rules name: FX-converted base price to cents (22), discount threshold and
  bonus aggregate to cents (16, 26), then the final unit price once from unrounded per-piece components (27).
  Breakdown fields are reports, not inputs. Bonus split: largest remainders (26); setup pool: the cent-allocation rule
  stated in the Ruestpools mail (25).
- **Reporting:** `surcharge_per_unit` is before discount and covers mass surcharge plus ordinary and allocated setup;
  setup and packaging are never discounted; blank = unanswered, `0.00` = known zero; `rebate_total` is per position.
- **Conditional discount (16):** threshold uses undiscounted scale prices, no surcharge or setup, inclusive; on failure
  0 %, never an older approval. Metal index: the rate whose window contains the scenario date (28).
- Positions are matched by number; extras or duplicates cost one position's share; money is compared to the cent.

## Runs, ranking, winning

Details live in `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `scoring.md`, `faq.md`. What bites:

- Test run (`atira test-run ./agent --follow`): 2 h, public data, shows per-part points, never on the leaderboard.
  Scored (`atira submit ./agent`): AI review, then one 20-minute run, one submission in flight per team (else 429).
- Time runs from the start of the run command to the accepted answer. 202 is final (even if wrong); 400 lists issues
  and the clock keeps running; validate against `answer_schema` first. Submit about 90 s before `expires_at` (the kit's
  `run.seconds_left` helps); platform docs only say "about a minute". A run without an answer scores 0.
- Setup has network and 5 min (untimed), but no run variables or secrets, and nothing it starts survives. The timed run
  reaches only the platform, sites and model proxy (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`, honour it in custom clients). Send your own
  User-Agent (default Python agents get 403 "Error 1010").
- `agent.json`: `setup`, `run`, `models` (list every hosted model used, e.g. `["qwen","clef"]`), `browsers` 1 to 4.
  Package: 20 MB compressed and uncompressed, 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, `.gitignore` honoured, no secrets inside.
  Own model keys are team secrets (names: capitals, digits, underscore, letter first, max 20, no platform names).
- Order: eligible (right tender reference), then quality 0 to 100, then lower cost x time (floors $0.01, 1 s). A wrong
  bid/no_bid decision costs quality, not eligibility (75 of 100 in a no_bid case). Weights: rule 29.
- Winners: private-dataset final run of our LATEST submission that PASSED review (not the best), then public
  leaderboard, then elegance. So: never tune to public-1; every passing `atira submit` replaces the final candidate,
  even a worse one, so confirm with the team first. `atira final --best-of 3` (before the final starts) allows three
  attempts (own-key cost up to 3x); private runs show no score breakdown.
- Models: hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`QWEN_BASE_URL/KEY`, 32 concurrent) and Clef (`CLEF_*`, 16 concurrent) are free
  but add a SIMULATED price to run cost; own-key calls are metered at provider prices through the proxy. Measured
  Qwen behaviour (thinking flag, schema cold start, caching) is in `docs/plan.md`.

## Dev loop

```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh    # CLI; the installer provides Node 24 if missing
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && atira login           # `atira upgrade` if a command is unknown

atira models proxy                       # terminal 1 (port 8765)
```

## Fair play (an AI reviewer rejects or flags these)

- No hardcoded scenario values (tender refs, material numbers, prices, discounts, logins, TANs), not even as defaults,
  fallbacks or in prompts. Facts the brief states for every scenario (e.g. the sales director's mailbox) are fine.
- No pre-solving, by you or an AI assistant, put into the package. Hand-derived expectations stay outside `agent/`.
- Must be agentic: a model chooses where to go, what to search and what matters. Rejected: a fixed click path (model
  unused or only a fallback), or a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation.
  Allowed helpers: parse a page or document the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate,
  validate, retry, fill forms. Several agents and parallel browsers are fine.
- Only the platform API, the four sites and the model proxy; no local models; no own browsers in the sandbox (use the
  provided 1 to 4, tabs and contexts are free).
- Do not write notes meant to steer the reviewer. Outcomes: passed; flagged (runs, but hidden from the leaderboard
  until an organizer passes it); rejected (no runs).

## The task and its traps

One signed bid, entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with a TAN from the webmail. Site ids are
public-1 names; the private set renames and re-splits sites, so never branch code on siteId, URL or layout.

| Site | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| Tender portal | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (the hub: quantity changes, withdrawals, scoped spec amendments, Konditionsgruppe, packaging, commitment and setup-pool keys), configurator |
| Supplier portal | Buyer's spec and revisions (oldest shown first; use the one marked current) |
| ERP | Materials and status, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity and scales, pieces per carton, allocation mass |
| Webmail | Director's discount approval, TAN, authority mails (look-alikes, superseded, archive) |

Read all 29 rules in `challenges/rfq.md` before writing prompts or tools. Highest-impact traps:

- **Authority and time (21):** per key, the latest record dated no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender
  reference, from the right sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation + bidder mailbox domain). Future-dated and
  unrelated records never apply; a failed condition does not revive an older record.
- **no_bid (3, 8, 16):** if any position has no exactly matching active material (after amendments and the "nutzbarer
  Weg" derivation, rule 20), send `no_bid`, no positions, `total_net` 0 (schema still requires `discount_percent`; a
  conditional approval means 0 %). Omitting positions is not a substitute (rule 9).
- **Sign and submit:** saving alone scores nothing. Partial bids use "Position auslassen" and are still signed.
- **Per position vs per material:** price scales per position; stock pooled per material (15); delivery commitments
  per position, only if the material matches and pooled demand is within the inclusive ceiling (24).
- **Rounding:** HALF_UP, at the steps the rules name: FX-converted base price to cents (22), discount threshold and
  bonus aggregate to cents (16, 26), then the final unit price once from unrounded per-piece components (27).
  Breakdown fields are reports, not inputs. Bonus split: largest remainders (26); setup pool: the cent-allocation rule
  stated in the Ruestpools mail (25).
- **Reporting:** `surcharge_per_unit` is before discount and covers mass surcharge plus ordinary and allocated setup;
  setup and packaging are never discounted; blank = unanswered, `0.00` = known zero; `rebate_total` is per position.
- **Conditional discount (16):** threshold uses undiscounted scale prices, no surcharge or setup, inclusive; on failure
  0 %, never an older approval. Metal index: the rate whose window contains the scenario date (28).
- Positions are matched by number; extras or duplicates cost one position's share; money is compared to the cent.

## Runs, ranking, winning

Details live in `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `scoring.md`, `faq.md`. What bites:

- Test run (`atira test-run ./agent --follow`): 2 h, public data, shows per-part points, never on the leaderboard.
  Scored (`atira submit ./agent`): AI review, then one 20-minute run, one submission in flight per team (else 429).
- Time runs from the start of the run command to the accepted answer. 202 is final (even if wrong); 400 lists issues
  and the clock keeps running; validate against `answer_schema` first. Submit about 90 s before `expires_at` (the kit's
  `run.seconds_left` helps); platform docs only say "about a minute". A run without an answer scores 0.
- Setup has network and 5 min (untimed), but no run variables or secrets, and nothing it starts survives. The timed run
  reaches only the platform, sites and model proxy (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`, honour it in custom clients). Send your own
  User-Agent (default Python agents get 403 "Error 1010").
- `agent.json`: `setup`, `run`, `models` (list every hosted model used, e.g. `["qwen","clef"]`), `browsers` 1 to 4.

  Own model keys are team secrets (names: capitals, digits, underscore, letter first, max 20, no platform names).
- Order: eligible (right tender reference), then quality 0 to 100, then lower cost x time (floors $0.01, 1 s). A wrong
  bid/no_bid decision costs quality, not eligibility (75 of 100 in a no_bid case). Weights: rule 29.
- Winners: private-dataset final run of our LATEST submission that PASSED review (not the best), then public

- Models: hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`QWEN_BASE_URL/KEY`, 32 concurrent) and Clef (`CLEF_*`, 16 concurrent) are free

"""
The agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

v2: read the brief, then the orchestrator (planner, findings board, research workers, verifier, calc) builds the
answer, and submit.py enters and signs the bid with it; without an answer every position is omitted, as in v1.
AGENT_RESEARCH=0 skips the research (the v1 path). See docs/plan.md.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import browsers
import loopwatch
import run as contract
from briefing import read_brief
from browser_tools import SiteSession
from orchestrator import Orchestrator
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
from submit import Mailbox, submit_bid
import tracing
from tracing import Trace

SAFETY_SECONDS = 90  # the answer must be in before the run expires
LOCAL_SECONDS = 20 * 60  # the scouting run does not expire; behave like a scored run


async def solve(task: dict, page, answer: dict | None = None,
                attributes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None = None) -> dict | None:
    """
    Enter the bid on the run's website (a "site" submission) and return None.

    `answer` (calc's BidResult.answer()) and `attributes` (per position, the chosen material's attributes) are what
    the bid worker enters; positions they do not give completely are omitted. Unless given, the orchestrator
    researches them; a research failure never costs the signed bid.
    """
    trace = Trace()
    loopwatch.Watchdog(activity=lambda: trace.last).start()  # a blocked loop or a silent run dumps its stacks
    left = min(contract.seconds_left(task), LOCAL_SECONDS)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + left - SAFETY_SECONDS
    # Sign in to every website while the model reads the brief: which one plays which part is only known after it.
    contexts = await browsers.more_contexts(page, len(task["access"]))
    sessions = {site["siteId"]: SiteSession(site, context, trace) for site, context in zip(task["access"], contexts)}
    started = asyncio.gather(*(session.start() for session in sessions.values()), return_exceptions=True)
    briefing, outcomes = await asyncio.gather(read_brief(task), started)
    # The run contract names the submission website; it wins over the model's reading of the brief.
    contract_site = (task.get("submission") or {}).get("siteId")
    if contract_site in sessions and contract_site != briefing.bid_site:
        trace.event("briefing", "bid_site_corrected", read=briefing.bid_site, contract=contract_site)
        briefing = briefing.model_copy(update={"bid_site": contract_site})
    trace.event("briefing", "done", **briefing.model_dump(exclude={"submission_steps"}))
    failed = {name for name, outcome in zip(sessions, outcomes) if isinstance(outcome, BaseException)}
    bid, mail = sessions[briefing.bid_site], sessions[briefing.mail_site]
    await asyncio.gather(*(session.start() for session in (bid, mail) if session.name in failed),
                         return_exceptions=True)  # submit_bid copes with a session that is still down
    if answer is None and os.environ.get("AGENT_RESEARCH", "1") != "0":
        answer, attributes = await research(task, briefing, contexts, trace, deadline)
    try:
        result = await submit_bid(bid, Mailbox(mail, briefing, deadline), briefing, deadline, answer, attributes)
    except Exception as error:  # never end without trying to sign: one more pass with what is on screen
        trace.event("submit", "crashed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}")
        result = await submit_bid(bid, Mailbox(mail, briefing, deadline), briefing, deadline, answer, attributes)
    trace.event("result", "done", result=result.model_dump() if result else None)
    return None


async def research(task: dict, briefing, contexts: list, trace: Trace, deadline: float
                   ) -> tuple[dict | None, dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None]:
    """The orchestrator's answer and material attributes; (None, None) when it fails or builds nothing."""
    answer, attributes, problems = None, None, []
    orchestrator = None
    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        orchestrator = Orchestrator(task, briefing, {s["siteId"]: c for s, c in zip(task["access"], contexts)},
                                    trace, deadline)
        problems = orchestrator.board.problems
        answer, _ = await orchestrator.run()
        attributes = orchestrator.attributes
    except Exception as error:  # the signed bid must never be lost to a research failure
        trace.event("orchestrator", "failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}")
    if answer is None and orchestrator is not None:  # still the reference, decision and any discount read
        answer = orchestrator.fallback_answer()
    trace.event("orchestrator", "done", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1), answer=answer,
                attributes=attributes, problems=problems[:30])
    path = Path(trace.path).with_name("answer.json")
    path.write_text(json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    print(f"Answer for the bid form written to {path}", flush=True)
    return answer, attributes


async def main() -> int:
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright)  # more browsers: browsers.connect(playwright, 1), ...
        try:
            answer = await solve(task, page)
        finally:  # the platform keeps only the last lines of a run's output: repeat the phases there
            tracing.print_summary()
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit through the API: the bid is entered on the website", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

summary against the requirements; the signing phase thinks only when that check fails or finds problems.
THINKING_FORM, THINKING_REVIEW (the check) and THINKING_SIGN override these defaults (see llm.thinking).
"""

class Mailbox:
    """The bidder's webmail, worked by the model on request; one request at a time in its tab."""

    def __init__(self, session: SiteSession, briefing: Briefing, deadline: float):
        self.session, self.briefing, self.deadline = session, briefing, deadline
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self.last_tan = ""

    async def address(self) -> str:
        """The bidder's own address, or "" when the webmail cannot tell: never an error that would stop the bid."""
        try:
            async with self.lock:
                found, _ = await run_worker(
                    self.session, "Find the email address of the mailbox you are signed in to (the bidder's own "
                    "address, usually shown as the signed-in account). Return it at once.",
                    MailboxAddress, deadline=self.deadline, max_steps=8, notes=False)
        except Exception as error:
            self.session.trace.event(self.session.name, "stopped", reason=f"address: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
            return ""
        return found.address if found else ""

    async def tan(self, answer: str = "") -> SigningTan | None:
        """
        The signing TAN just requested. The sites run on the scenario's clock, so "newest" is the highest request
        number or the top of the list, never a wall-clock time. `answer` is what the bid website said to the request
        (it may name the request), so the mail worker can pick that very message.
        """
        older = f" The TAN {self.last_tan} you returned before is no longer valid." if self.last_tan else ""
        said = (f" The bid website answered the request with: {answer!r}; pick the message for that request."
                if answer else "")
        try:
            return await self._tan(older, said, answer)
        except Exception as error:  # the bid worker asks again; an error here must not stop the bid
            self.session.trace.event(self.session.name, "stopped", reason=f"tan: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
            return None

    async def _tan(self, older: str, said: str, answer: str) -> SigningTan | None:
        async with self.lock:
            async with self.session.lock:  # the list the tab shows predates the request: load it again
                await self.session.revive()
                await self.session._goto(self.session.page.url)
            found, _ = await run_worker(
                self.session, f"A new signing TAN for tender {self.briefing.tender_reference} was just requested."
                f"{said} Open the newest signing TAN message for exactly this tender reference (the highest "
                "request number; new TAN messages are listed without a search, newest first; reload the list once "
                "if it is not there yet), copy the TAN from its text and return it at once. If a preview pane "
                f"stays empty, open the message's own page through its link.{older}",
                SigningTan, context=answer, deadline=self.deadline, max_steps=10, notes=False)
        if found:
            self.last_tan = found.tan
        return found


class FormAction(BaseModel):
    ref: str = Field(description="The element's ref in the latest view")
    action: Literal["fill", "select", "check", "uncheck", "click"]
    value: str = Field("", description="fill: the text to type; select: the option's visible text, exactly as the "
                                       "view lists it; empty for check, uncheck and click")


async def _perform(element, step: FormAction) -> None:
    if step.action == "fill":
        await element.fill(step.value, timeout=2000)
    elif step.action == "select":
        if not step.value:
            raise ValueError("select needs the option's visible text as value")
        try:
            await element.select_option(label=step.value, timeout=2000)
        except Exception:
            await element.select_option(step.value, timeout=2000)
    elif step.action in ("check", "uncheck"):
        await element.set_checked(step.action == "check", timeout=2000)
    else:
        try:
            await element.click(timeout=5000)
        except Exception:
            await element.evaluate("e => e.click()")


async def fill_in(ctx: RunContext[Deps], actions: list[FormAction]) -> str:
    """
    Do several actions on the current page in one go, in this order: fill textboxes, choose options, tick boxes,
    or click buttons that keep you on this page (such as one per table row). Use refs from the latest view. It
    stops at the first action that fails or that leaves the page, and returns the new view. Put a button that
    moves to the next step only last, or click it on its own.
    """
    session = ctx.deps.session
    done: list[str] = []
    stop = ""
    async with session.lock:
        page, url, windows = session.page, session.page.url, len(session.pages)
        for step in actions:
            element = await locate(page, step.ref)
            if element is None:
                stop = f"no element {step.ref} (the page changed; use the new view)"
                break
            try:
                await _perform(element, step)
            except Exception as error:
                stop = f"{step.action} {step.ref} {step.value!r} failed: {str(error).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
                break
            done.append(f"{step.action} {step.ref}")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.15)
            if page.is_closed() or page.url != url or len(session.pages) != windows:
                if step is not actions[-1]:
                    stop = "the page changed after it; the remaining actions were not done"
                break
        await asyncio.sleep(0.25)
        await session.settle()
        session.trace.event(session.name, "action", action="fill_in", done=done, stop=stop,
                            asked=[step.model_dump() for step in actions])
        view = await session.look()
    report = f"Done: {', '.join(done) or 'nothing'}." + (f" Stopped: {stop}." if stop else "")
    return f"{report}\n\n{view}"


class PositionDesk:
    """
    The bid worker's tools for the positions: enter the calculated values of the position the model says is on
    screen, and total what was entered. Positions that fail are left for the model to omit.
    """

    def __init__(self, entries: dict[str, dict], deadline: float):
        self.entries, self.deadline = entries, deadline
        self.plan = FillPlan()
        self.failures: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.entered: set[str] = set()
        self.choices: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        self.next_button = ""

    @property
    def tools(self) -> tuple:
        return (self.configure_position, self.net_total) if self.entries else ()

    async def configure_position(self, ctx: RunContext[Deps], position: str, fields: dict[str, str] | None = None,
                                 confirm_button: str = "", next_button: str = "",
                                 choices: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str:
        """
        Enter all values of the position the form shows now and, once all are in, save it and go on with the form's
        next/continue button. `position`: its number as the page shows it. `fields`: control label (exactly as in
        your view) -> value name; needed on the first call, later calls reuse it. `confirm_button`: label of the
        button that applies a choice so the next choice opens. `next_button`: label of the button that saves the
        position and goes on (never the one that omits or adds a position); needed once. `choices`: only when a
        call reported that no option equals an attribute: control label -> the option that means the same.
        """
        session, plan, position = ctx.deps.session, self.plan, position.strip()
        known = set().union(*self.entries.values()) - {"position"}
        if fields:  # later calls add to or correct the mapping, they never drop what was mapped before
            given = {label: name.strip() for label, name in fields.items()}
            unknown = sorted({name for name in given.values() if name not in known})
            if unknown:
                return f"Unknown value names {unknown}; use only: {', '.join(sorted(known))}. Call again."
            plan.fields = {label: name for label, name in plan.fields.items() if name not in given.values()}
            plan.fields.update(given)
        if confirm_button:
            plan.confirm = confirm_button
        if next_button:
            self.next_button = next_button
        entry = self.entries.get(position)
        if entry is None:
            return (f"No values for position {position!r}: leave it out with the form's option to omit a position. "
                    + self.so_far(session))
        if not plan.fields:
            return "Give fields (control label -> value name) for the controls of this form first."
        if self.failures.get(position, 0) >= 3:
            return (f"Position {position} failed three times: leave it out with the form's option to omit a "
                    f"position. {self.so_far(session)}")
        if time.monotonic() > self.deadline - SIGNING_RESERVE:
            return ("Time is short: leave this and every remaining position out and go on to signing. "
                    + self.so_far(session))
        async with session.lock:
            if not position_on_page(await session.look(), position):
                return (f"Position {position} is not on the page now. Configure the position the page shows, by "
                        "its own number.")
            log: list[str] = []
            try:
                remembered = self.choices.setdefault(position, {})
                remembered.update(choices or {})  # a revisit of the position needs the same picks
                error = await fill_position(session, entry, plan, log, remembered)
            except Exception as exc:  # a slow or changed page: the model decides to retry or omit
                error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
            moved = ""
            if not error and self.next_button:  # the model named the button; clicking it is the mechanical part
                view = await session.look()
                ref, why = find_control(view, self.next_button, ("button",))
                target = await locate(session.page, ref) if ref else None
                if target is None:
                    moved = f" Could not save it: {why}; click the form's next/continue button yourself."
                else:
                    await target.click(timeout=5000)
                    await session.settle()
                    moved = f" Saved with {self.next_button!r}; the page below is the form's next step."
            session.trace.event(session.name, "configure_position", position=position, done=log, error=error,
                                moved=moved)
            view = await session.look()
        if error:
            self.failures[position] = self.failures.get(position, 0) + 1
            self.entered.discard(position)
            return (f"Position {position} not fully entered: {error}. Entered so far: {'; '.join(log) or 'nothing'}. "
                    "Fix the mapping and call again, or leave the position out with the form's option to omit "
                    f"it. {self.so_far(session)}\n\n{view}")
        self.entered.add(position)
        then = moved or " Check it, then save and continue with the form's next/continue button."
        return f"Position {position} entered: {'; '.join(log)}.{then} {self.so_far(session)}\n\n{view}"

    def so_far(self, session: SiteSession) -> str:
        """The running net total, told after every position so the totals step needs no arithmetic."""
        total = german(self.total())
        session.seen += "\n" + total  # our own figure: let the worker's result mention it
        entered = ", ".join(sorted(self.entered, key=position_key)) or "none"
        return f"Net total of the positions entered so far: {total} ({entered}); enter the latest such figure."

    def entry_total(self, position: str) -> Decimal:
        entry = self.entries[position]
        return Decimal(str(entry["quantity"])) * Decimal(str(entry["unit_price"]))

    def total(self, omitted: set[str] = frozenset()) -> Decimal:
        return sum((self.entry_total(p) for p in self.entered - omitted), Decimal(0))

    def expected(self) -> str:
        """What the review should show for each position entered, for the summary check and the signing pass."""
        lines = []
        for p in sorted(self.entered, key=position_key):
            e = self.entries[p]
            extra = ", ".join(f"{label} {german(e[key])}" for key, label in (
                ("base_unit_price", "base price"), ("surcharge_per_unit", "surcharge per piece"),
                ("packaging_per_unit", "packaging per piece"), ("rebate_total", "bonus for the position"))
                if e.get(key) is not None)
            lines.append(f"  - position {p}: material {e['material_number']}, quantity {e['quantity']}, net unit "
                         f"price {german(e['unit_price'])}, lead time {e['lead_time_weeks']} weeks"
                         + (f", {extra}" if extra else ""))
        return "\n".join(lines)

    async def net_total(self, omitted: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
        """
        The bid's net total in German format: quantity x unit price summed over the positions entered with
        configure_position(), minus any listed in `omitted` (positions you left out after all).
        """
        dropped = {p.strip() for p in omitted or []}
        return f"{german(self.total(dropped))} (positions {', '.join(sorted(self.entered - dropped)) or 'none'})"


def _positions(answer: dict | None, desk: PositionDesk, filled: bool) -> str:
    """
    The decision and position part of the requirements: before the form phase, how to enter them; after it, what
    the review must show (the positions actually entered, all others omitted, the total of the entered ones).
    """
    discount = german((answer or {}).get("discount_percent") or 0)
    if answer and answer.get("decision") == "no_bid":
        return ("- decision: no bid: choose the form's declaration that you do not submit an offer (not a main or "
                f"alternative offer); no positions;\n- discount {discount} and net total 0,00;")
    head = "- decision: bid (main offer, not an alternative offer);\n"
    if filled and desk.entered:
        return head + (f"- exactly {len(desk.entered)} position(s) entered, each with these values:\n"
                       f"{desk.expected()}\n"
                       "- every other position omitted, and no added or extra position;\n"
                       f"- discount {discount} and net total {german(desk.total())} (German number format; never a "
                       "gross amount);")
    if not desk.entries:
        return head + ("- leave every position out with the form's option to omit a position (where the form shows "
                       "one position per step, omit each in turn); do not configure materials, prices or lead times, "
                       f"and never use options that add positions;\n- discount {discount} and net total 0,00 (German "
                       "number format);")
    names = sorted({key for entry in desk.entries.values() for key in entry} - {"position"})
    return head + f"""- enter exactly these positions: {', '.join(sorted(desk.entries))}. The form shows one position
  at a time, in its own order. On every position page, first call configure_position() with the number the page
  shows: it enters all values of a position of this bid and saves it with the next/continue button you name, or
  tells you to omit it. Never pick options or type position values yourself;
- configure_position() needs, once, which control takes which value: map each control's label (as your view shows
  it) to one of these value names: {', '.join(names)}. Choices that open further choices (attributes of the
  material) map to the attribute with the same meaning; the material/catalogue number control to material_number;
  unit price, base price, surcharge, packaging and the bonus or rebate for the whole position to unit_price,
  base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total; lead time to lead_time_weeks. Leave out
  controls with no matching value. Also name the button that applies a choice so the next one opens, and the
  button that saves the position and goes on to the next step (not the ones that omit or add a position);
- leave out, with the form's option to omit a position, every other position and any position where
  configure_position() reports a problem it cannot resolve. Never use options that add positions; if the form
  shows an extra position you did not ask for, remove it or leave it out;
- discount {discount}; net total: the latest figure configure_position() reports for the positions entered so
  far (net_total() repeats it; pass positions you entered but left out after all). Enter both exactly as given
  (German number format), never a sum you work out yourself, a gross amount or a sum the page proposes;"""


def _requirements(briefing: Briefing, email: str, answer: dict | None = None, desk: PositionDesk | None = None,
                  filled: bool = False) -> str:
    contact = repr(email) if email else "the contact email from bidder_contact_email()"
    return f"""{_positions(answer, desk or PositionDesk({}, 0), filled)}
- register with company name {briefing.company_name!r}, VAT id {briefing.vat_id!r} and contact email {contact};
- tick the form's acknowledgement of the tender documents (no need to open them), but do not tick declarations
  that make your own terms and conditions apply."""


class SummaryCheck(BaseModel):
    matches: bool = Field(description="True when the page contradicts none of the requirements")
    problems: str = Field(description="Each requirement the page visibly contradicts, with what the page shows; "
                                      "'' if none")


async def check_summary(view: str, requirements: str) -> SummaryCheck | None:
    """One model call (thinking off by default, THINKING_REVIEW) on the review page before signing."""
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=SummaryCheck, retries=2,
                  model_settings=llm.settings(llm.thinking("review", False)),
                  instructions="You check the final review page of a bid against the bidder's requirements before "
                               "it is signed. Report only what the page visibly contradicts (a wrong or missing "
                               "value, a position that is not omitted, an extra position, a wrong offer type); "
                               "requirements the page does not show at all are no problem.")
    try:
        result = await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(f"Requirements:\n{requirements}\n\nReview page:\n{view}"), 90)
    except Exception:  # a failed check means the signing worker checks the page itself, with thinking on
        return None
    return result.output


async def submit_bid(bid_session: SiteSession, mailbox: Mailbox, briefing: Briefing, deadline: float,
                     answer: dict | None = None, attributes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None = None
                     ) -> SubmissionResult | None:
    """
    Enter the calculated `answer` (calc's BidResult.answer()), sign and submit it. Positions the answer does not
    give completely, or that fail to enter, are omitted; without an answer every position is omitted (discount 0,
    total 0). `attributes` holds per position number the chosen material's attributes (e.g. its dimensions), which
    the form's choices lead through to the catalogue number.
    """
    desk = PositionDesk(complete_positions(answer or {}, attributes), deadline)
    address = asyncio.create_task(mailbox.address())
    try:  # the lookup takes a step or two; knowing the address up front saves the bid worker a round trip
        email = await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(address), ADDRESS_WAIT)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        email = ""
    if email:
        bid_session.seen += "\n" + email  # it comes from another website; let results use it

    async def bidder_contact_email(reason: str = "") -> str:
        """The bidder's contact email address, read from the bidder's own webmail."""
        found = await address
        bid_session.seen += "\n" + found
        return found or "not found: the webmail did not show it"

    async def request_signing_tan(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str) -> str:
        """
        Click the website's control that requests the signing TAN (its ref in the latest view), then fetch that
        TAN from the bidder's webmail. Returns the page after the request and the TAN: enter it right away (it is
        valid for five minutes, and any new request invalidates it).
        """
        before = set(bid_session.view.splitlines())
        view = await browser_tools.click(ctx, ref)

171	    """The bidder's webmail, worked by the model on request; one request at a time in its tab."""

173	    def __init__(self, session: SiteSession, briefing: Briefing, deadline: float):
174	        self.session, self.briefing, self.deadline = session, briefing, deadline
175	        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()
176	        self.last_tan = ""

178	    async def address(self) -> str:
179	        """The bidder's own address, or "" when the webmail cannot tell: never an error that would stop the bid."""
180	        try:
181	            async with self.lock:
182	                found, _ = await run_worker(
183	                    self.session, "Find the email address of the mailbox you are signed in to (the bidder's own "
184	                    "address, usually shown as the signed-in account). Return it at once.",
185	                    MailboxAddress, deadline=self.deadline, max_steps=8, notes=False)
186	        except Exception as error:
187	            self.session.trace.event(self.session.name, "stopped", reason=f"address: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
188	            return ""

191	    async def tan(self, answer: str = "") -> SigningTan | None:
192	        """
193	        The signing TAN just requested. The sites run on the scenario's clock, so "newest" is the highest request
194	        number or the top of the list, never a wall-clock time. `answer` is what the bid website said to the request
195	        (it may name the request), so the mail worker can pick that very message.
196	        """
197	        older = f" The TAN {self.last_tan} you returned before is no longer valid." if self.last_tan else ""
198	        said = (f" The bid website answered the request with: {answer!r}; pick the message for that request."
199	                if answer else "")
200	        try:
201	            return await self._tan(older, said, answer)
202	        except Exception as error:  # the bid worker asks again; an error here must not stop the bid
203	            self.session.trace.event(self.session.name, "stopped", reason=f"tan: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
204	            return None

206	    async def _tan(self, older: str, said: str, answer: str) -> SigningTan | None:
207	        async with self.lock:
208	            async with self.session.lock:  # the list the tab shows predates the request: load it again
209	                await self.session.revive()
210	                await self.session._goto(self.session.page.url)
211	            found, _ = await run_worker(
212	                self.session, f"A new signing TAN for tender {self.briefing.tender_reference} was just requested."
213	                f"{said} Open the newest signing TAN message for exactly this tender reference (the highest "
214	                "request number; new TAN messages are listed without a search, newest first; reload the list once "
215	                "if it is not there yet), copy the TAN from its text and return it at once. If a preview pane "
216	                f"stays empty, open the message's own page through its link.{older}",
217	                SigningTan, context=answer, deadline=self.deadline, max_steps=10, notes=False)
218	        if found:
219	            self.last_tan = found.tan
220	        return found

230	async def _perform(element, step: FormAction) -> None:
231	    if step.action == "fill":
232	        await element.fill(step.value, timeout=2000)
233	    elif step.action == "select":
234	        if not step.value:
235	            raise ValueError("select needs the option's visible text as value")
236	        try:
237	            await element.select_option(label=step.value, timeout=2000)
238	        except Exception:
239	            await element.select_option(step.value, timeout=2000)
240	    elif step.action in ("check", "uncheck"):
241	        await element.set_checked(step.action == "check", timeout=2000)

244	            await element.click(timeout=5000)

249	async def fill_in(ctx: RunContext[Deps], actions: list[FormAction]) -> str:
250	    """
251	    Do several actions on the current page in one go, in this order: fill textboxes, choose options, tick boxes,
252	    or click buttons that keep you on this page (such as one per table row). Use refs from the latest view. It
253	    stops at the first action that fails or that leaves the page, and returns the new view. Put a button that
254	    moves to the next step only last, or click it on its own.
255	    """
256	    session = ctx.deps.session
257	    done: list[str] = []
258	    stop = ""
259	    async with session.lock:
260	        page, url, windows = session.page, session.page.url, len(session.pages)
261	        for step in actions:
262	            element = await locate(page, step.ref)
263	            if element is None:
264	                stop = f"no element {step.ref} (the page changed; use the new view)"
265	                break
266	            try:
267	                await _perform(element, step)
268	            except Exception as error:
269	                stop = f"{step.action} {step.ref} {step.value!r} failed: {str(error).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
270	                break
271	            done.append(f"{step.action} {step.ref}")
272	            await asyncio.sleep(0.15)
273	            if page.is_closed() or page.url != url or len(session.pages) != windows:
274	                if step is not actions[-1]:
275	                    stop = "the page changed after it; the remaining actions were not done"
276	                break
277	        await asyncio.sleep(0.25)
278	        await session.settle()
279	        session.trace.event(session.name, "action", action="fill_in", done=done, stop=stop,
280	                            asked=[step.model_dump() for step in actions])
281	        view = await session.look()
282	    report = f"Done: {', '.join(done) or 'nothing'}." + (f" Stopped: {stop}." if stop else "")
283	    return f"{report}\n\n{view}"

286	class PositionDesk:
287	    """
288	    The bid worker's tools for the positions: enter the calculated values of the position the model says is on
289	    screen, and total what was entered. Positions that fail are left for the model to omit.
290	    """
291	
292	    def __init__(self, entries: dict[str, dict], deadline: float):
293	        self.entries, self.deadline = entries, deadline
294	        self.plan = FillPlan()
295	        self.failures: dict[str, int] = {}
296	        self.entered: set[str] = set()
297	        self.choices: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
298	        self.next_button = ""
299	
300	    @property
301	    def tools(self) -> tuple:
302	        return (self.configure_position, self.net_total) if self.entries else ()
303	
304	    async def configure_position(self, ctx: RunContext[Deps], position: str, fields: dict[str, str] | None = None,
305	                                 confirm_button: str = "", next_button: str = "",
306	                                 choices: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str:
307	        """
308	        Enter all values of the position the form shows now and, once all are in, save it and go on with the form's
309	        next/continue button. `position`: its number as the page shows it. `fields`: control label (exactly as in
310	        your view) -> value name; needed on the first call, later calls reuse it. `confirm_button`: label of the
311	        button that applies a choice so the next choice opens. `next_button`: label of the button that saves the
312	        position and goes on (never the one that omits or adds a position); needed once. `choices`: only when a
313	        call reported that no option equals an attribute: control label -> the option that means the same.
314	        """
315	        session, plan, position = ctx.deps.session, self.plan, position.strip()
316	        known = set().union(*self.entries.values()) - {"position"}
317	        if fields:  # later calls add to or correct the mapping, they never drop what was mapped before
318	            given = {label: name.strip() for label, name in fields.items()}
319	            unknown = sorted({name for name in given.values() if name not in known})
320	            if unknown:
321	                return f"Unknown value names {unknown}; use only: {', '.join(sorted(known))}. Call again."
322	            plan.fields = {label: name for label, name in plan.fields.items() if name not in given.values()}
323	            plan.fields.update(given)
324	        if confirm_button:
325	            plan.confirm = confirm_button
326	        if next_button:
327	            self.next_button = next_button
328	        entry = self.entries.get(position)
329	        if entry is None:
330	            return (f"No values for position {position!r}: leave it out with the form's option to omit a position. "
331	                    + self.so_far(session))
332	        if not plan.fields:
333	            return "Give fields (control label -> value name) for the controls of this form first."
334	        if self.failures.get(position, 0) >= 3:
335	            return (f"Position {position} failed three times: leave it out with the form's option to omit a "
336	                    f"position. {self.so_far(session)}")
337	        if time.monotonic() > self.deadline - SIGNING_RESERVE:
338	            return ("Time is short: leave this and every remaining position out and go on to signing. "
339	                    + self.so_far(session))
340	        async with session.lock:
341	            if not position_on_page(await session.look(), position):
342	                return (f"Position {position} is not on the page now. Configure the position the page shows, by "
343	                        "its own number.")
344	            log: list[str] = []
345	            try:
346	                remembered = self.choices.setdefault(position, {})
347	                remembered.update(choices or {})  # a revisit of the position needs the same picks
348	                error = await fill_position(session, entry, plan, log, remembered)
349	            except Exception as exc:  # a slow or changed page: the model decides to retry or omit
350	                error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
351	            moved = ""
352	            if not error and self.next_button:  # the model named the button; clicking it is the mechanical part
353	                view = await session.look()
354	                ref, why = find_control(view, self.next_button, ("button",))
355	                target = await locate(session.page, ref) if ref else None
356	                if target is None:
357	                    moved = f" Could not save it: {why}; click the form's next/continue button yourself."
358	                else:
359	                    await target.click(timeout=5000)
360	                    await session.settle()
361	                    moved = f" Saved with {self.next_button!r}; the page below is the form's next step."
362	            session.trace.event(session.name, "configure_position", position=position, done=log, error=error,
363	                                moved=moved)
364	            view = await session.look()
365	        if error:
366	            self.failures[position] = self.failures.get(position, 0) + 1
367	            self.entered.discard(position)
368	            return (f"Position {position} not fully entered: {error}. Entered so far: {'; '.join(log) or 'nothing'}. "
369	                    "Fix the mapping and call again, or leave the position out with the form's option to omit "
370	                    f"it. {self.so_far(session)}\n\n{view}")
371	        self.entered.add(position)
372	        then = moved or " Check it, then save and continue with the form's next/continue button."
373	        return f"Position {position} entered: {'; '.join(log)}.{then} {self.so_far(session)}\n\n{view}"
374	
375	    def so_far(self, session: SiteSession) -> str:
376	        """The running net total, told after every position so the totals step needs no arithmetic."""
377	        total = german(self.total())
378	        session.seen += "\n" + total  # our own figure: let the worker's result mention it
379	        entered = ", ".join(sorted(self.entered, key=position_key)) or "none"
380	        return f"Net total of the positions entered so far: {total} ({entered}); enter the latest such figure."
381	
382	    def entry_total(self, position: str) -> Decimal:
383	        entry = self.entries[position]
384	        return Decimal(str(entry["quantity"])) * Decimal(str(entry["unit_price"]))
385	
386	    def total(self, omitted: set[str] = frozenset()) -> Decimal:
387	        return sum((self.entry_total(p) for p in self.entered - omitted), Decimal(0))
388	
389	    def expected(self) -> str:
390	        """What the review should show for each position entered, for the summary check and the signing pass."""
391	        lines = []
392	        for p in sorted(self.entered, key=position_key):
393	            e = self.entries[p]
394	            extra = ", ".join(f"{label} {german(e[key])}" for key, label in (
395	                ("base_unit_price", "base price"), ("surcharge_per_unit", "surcharge per piece"),
396	                ("packaging_per_unit", "packaging per piece"), ("rebate_total", "bonus for the position"))
397	                if e.get(key) is not None)
398	            lines.append(f"  - position {p}: material {e['material_number']}, quantity {e['quantity']}, net unit "
399	                         f"price {german(e['unit_price'])}, lead time {e['lead_time_weeks']} weeks"
400	                         + (f", {extra}" if extra else ""))
401	        return "\n".join(lines)
402	
403	    async def net_total(self, omitted: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
404	        """
405	        The bid's net total in German format: quantity x unit price summed over the positions entered with
406	        configure_position(), minus any listed in `omitted` (positions you left out after all).
407	        """
408	        dropped = {p.strip() for p in omitted or []}
409	        return f"{german(self.total(dropped))} (positions {', '.join(sorted(self.entered - dropped)) or 'none'})"
410

412	def _positions(answer: dict | None, desk: PositionDesk, filled: bool) -> str:
413	    """
414	    The decision and position part of the requirements: before the form phase, how to enter them; after it, what
415	    the review must show (the positions actually entered, all others omitted, the total of the entered ones).
416	    """
417	    discount = german((answer or {}).get("discount_percent") or 0)
418	    if answer and answer.get("decision") == "no_bid":
419	        return ("- decision: no bid: choose the form's declaration that you do not submit an offer (not a main or "
420	                f"alternative offer); no positions;\n- discount {discount} and net total 0,00;")
421	    head = "- decision: bid (main offer, not an alternative offer);\n"
422	    if filled and desk.entered:
423	        return head + (f"- exactly {len(desk.entered)} position(s) entered, each with these values:\n"
424	                       f"{desk.expected()}\n"
425	                       "- every other position omitted, and no added or extra position;\n"
426	                       f"- discount {discount} and net total {german(desk.total())} (German number format; never a "
427	                       "gross amount);")
428	    if not desk.entries:
429	        return head + ("- leave every position out with the form's option to omit a position (where the form shows "
430	                       "one position per step, omit each in turn); do not configure materials, prices or lead times, "
431	                       f"and never use options that add positions;\n- discount {discount} and net total 0,00 (German "
432	                       "number format);")
433	    names = sorted({key for entry in desk.entries.values() for key in entry} - {"position"})
434	    return head + f"""- enter exactly these positions: {', '.join(sorted(desk.entries))}. The form shows one position
435	  at a time, in its own order. On every position page, first call configure_position() with the number the page
436	  shows: it enters all values of a position of this bid and saves it with the next/continue button you name, or
437	  tells you to omit it. Never pick options or type position values yourself;
438	- configure_position() needs, once, which control takes which value: map each control's label (as your view shows
439	  it) to one of these value names: {', '.join(names)}. Choices that open further choices (attributes of the
440	  material) map to the attribute with the same meaning; the material/catalogue number control to material_number;
441	  unit price, base price, surcharge, packaging and the bonus or rebate for the whole position to unit_price,
442	  base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total; lead time to lead_time_weeks. Leave out
443	  controls with no matching value. Also name the button that applies a choice so the next one opens, and the
444	  button that saves the position and goes on to the next step (not the ones that omit or add a position);
445	- leave out, with the form's option to omit a position, every other position and any position where
446	  configure_position() reports a problem it cannot resolve. Never use options that add positions; if the form
447	  shows an extra position you did not ask for, remove it or leave it out;
448	- discount {discount}; net total: the latest figure configure_position() reports for the positions entered so
449	  far (net_total() repeats it; pass positions you entered but left out after all). Enter both exactly as given
450	  (German number format), never a sum you work out yourself, a gross amount or a sum the page proposes;"""
451

455	    contact = repr(email) if email else "the contact email from bidder_contact_email()"

457	- register with company name {briefing.company_name!r}, VAT id {briefing.vat_id!r} and contact email {contact};
458	- tick the form's acknowledgement of the tender documents (no need to open them), but do not tick declarations
459	  that make your own terms and conditions apply."""

463	    matches: bool = Field(description="True when the page contradicts none of the requirements")

468	async def check_summary(view: str, requirements: str) -> SummaryCheck | None:
469	    """One model call (thinking off by default, THINKING_REVIEW) on the review page before signing."""
470	    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=SummaryCheck, retries=2,
471	                  model_settings=llm.settings(llm.thinking("review", False)),
472	                  instructions="You check the final review page of a bid against the bidder's requirements before "
473	                               "it is signed. Report only what the page visibly contradicts (a wrong or missing "
474	                               "value, a position that is not omitted, an extra position, a wrong offer type); "
475	                               "requirements the page does not show at all are no problem.")
476	    try:
477	        result = await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(f"Requirements:\n{requirements}\n\nReview page:\n{view}"), 90)
478	    except Exception:  # a failed check means the signing worker checks the page itself, with thinking on
479	        return None
480	    return result.output

483	async def submit_bid(bid_session: SiteSession, mailbox: Mailbox, briefing: Briefing, deadline: float,
484	                     answer: dict | None = None, attributes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None = None
485	                     ) -> SubmissionResult | None:
486	    """
487	    Enter the calculated `answer` (calc's BidResult.answer()), sign and submit it. Positions the answer does not
488	    give completely, or that fail to enter, are omitted; without an answer every position is omitted (discount 0,
489	    total 0). `attributes` holds per position number the chosen material's attributes (e.g. its dimensions), which
490	    the form's choices lead through to the catalogue number.
491	    """
492	    desk = PositionDesk(complete_positions(answer or {}, attributes), deadline)
493	    address = asyncio.create_task(mailbox.address())
494	    try:  # the lookup takes a step or two; knowing the address up front saves the bid worker a round trip
495	        email = await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(address), ADDRESS_WAIT)
496	    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
497	        email = ""
498	    if email:
499	        bid_session.seen += "\n" + email  # it comes from another website; let results use it
500	
501	    async def bidder_contact_email(reason: str = "") -> str:
502	        """The bidder's contact email address, read from the bidder's own webmail."""
503	        found = await address
504	        bid_session.seen += "\n" + found
505	        return found or "not found: the webmail did not show it"
506	
507	    async def request_signing_tan(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str) -> str:
508	        """
509	        Click the website's control that requests the signing TAN (its ref in the latest view), then fetch that
510	        TAN from the bidder's webmail. Returns the page after the request and the TAN: enter it right away (it is
511	        valid for five minutes, and any new request invalidates it).
512	        """
513	        before = set(bid_session.view.splitlines())
514	        view = await browser_tools.click(ctx, ref)
515	        answer = " ".join(line.strip() for line in bid_session.view.splitlines()
516	                          if line.strip() and line not in before and "[e" not in line)[:400]
517	        found = await mailbox.tan(answer)
518	        if not found:
519	            return f"{view}\n\nNo TAN found in the webmail. Request a new TAN with this tool again."
520	        bid_session.seen += "\n" + found.tan
521	        return f"{view}\n\nTAN from the webmail: {found.tan} (message {found.subject!r}, received {found.received})."
522	
523	    tools = ((bidder_contact_email,) if not email else ()) + desk.tools
524	    batch = os.environ.get("AGENT_FILL_IN", "1") != "0"
525	    if batch:
526	        tools += (fill_in,)
527	    several = ("Enter everything a page asks for with one fill_in() call (all its fields, boxes and per-row "
528	               "buttons), then move on.\n" if batch else "")
529	    form_goal = f"""Fill in the bid for tender {briefing.tender_reference} on this website, following the brief's
530	submission steps below, up to the final review and signing step. Every value of this bid is already researched
531	and calculated; you only enter it: do not open documents, questions or other pages to check or research anything.
532	For this bid:
533	{_requirements(briefing, email, answer, desk)}
534	{several}Stop at the final review with the signing step: do not request a TAN and do not submit there.
535	Return as soon as that page shows. Refs change with every view: read a button's label in the latest view before
536	clicking it.
537	
538	Brief's submission steps:
539	{briefing.submission_steps}"""
540	    left = deadline - time.monotonic()
541	    # the form never eats the signing reserve; with little time left, half of it still goes to the form
542	    form_deadline = deadline - SIGNING_RESERVE if left > SIGNING_RESERVE + 90 else time.monotonic() + left / 2
543	    ready, _ = await run_worker(bid_session, form_goal, FormReady, deadline=form_deadline,
544	                                max_steps=45 + 3 * len(desk.entries), notes=False,
545	                                thinking=llm.thinking("form", False), tools=tools)
546	
547	    requirements = _requirements(briefing, email, answer, desk, filled=True)
548	    check = await check_summary(bid_session.view, requirements) if ready and ready.at_signing_step else None
549	    bid_session.trace.event(bid_session.name, "summary_check", **(check.model_dump() if check else {}))
550	    if check and check.matches:
551	        task = ("The form was filled in up to the signing step by an earlier pass, and its summary was checked "
552	                "against the requirements below; the current view shows it.")
553	    elif check:
554	        task = (f"The form was filled in up to the signing step by an earlier pass. A quick check of the summary "
555	                f"(which can be wrong) reported: {check.problems} Fix it only if the fix is on the current page; "
556	                f"never go back to earlier steps (that clears them). If it cannot be fixed here, sign anyway: a "
